newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CPI improvement disappoints Australian bonds.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CPI improvement disappoints Australian bonds.

text.p: *Australian bonds erase opening gains, with 10-years closing down on day, as long market sells when CPI comes in as expected.
*CPI rises 1.5 percent over 1996, underlying rate up 2.1 pct
*Treasury revises 96/97 borrowing task up to A$10.2 bln
Australian bonds struggled, with 10-year bonds falling into negative territory, as a long market sold off on news of that fall in inflation had only met expectations rather than exceeded them.
"People obviously got long in anticipation of a fantastic CPI result, and in the end they just got an excellent one," Bankers Trust interest rate strategist Rory Robertson said.

Australia's CPI rose just 0.2 percent in the December quarter, to be 1.5 percent higher over the year. It was the lowest annual rise since the March 1994 quarter, and was slightly under median expectations.

The underlying rate, the focus of monetary policy, rose 0.4 percent to be 2.1 percent higher over the year, its lowest annual rise since the March 1995 quarter. The underlying inflation figures were spot on market expectations.
Bonds, which had built on overnight gains from the open, sold to their lows on the news as profits were taken both on the early gains and on the narrowing in the spreads to U.S. bonds.

While a negative on the day, because the most bullish expectations went unrealised, analysts said the result should be supportive of bonds longer term as it confirmed Australia's low inflation status.
"The data confirms the optimism of the government and the RBA on the inflation front," Hambros Australia fixed income economist Su-Lin Ong said.

U.S. Treasuries weakening further in Tokyo did not help the sell tone in the market, traders said, and neither did the fall of the Australian dollar through key support at US$0.7680 to a 10 month low against the U.S. dollar.
As well, the Australian Treasury announced its funding task for 1996/97 to June 30 had been lifted to around A$10.2 billion from the previous forecast of A$7.0 billion.

While bonds softened a little further after this news, it was essentially already in the market after the government had announced on Tuesday a A$2.9 billion deterioration in the budget position for the current financial year, traders said.
Spreads finished mixed after selling off on CPI data.
Earlier spreads had narrowed markedly, with the spread to U.S. bonds moving under 75 basis points as the market got bullish ahead of the CPI data.
